config.title: FUNDA — Tooltip Directive

intro.title: FUNDA — Tooltip Directive
intro.body: In this lesson you will build a Tooltip Directive — an attribute directive that can be applied to any element to show a floating tooltip on hover. The directive uses @HostListener for mouseenter and mouseleave, Renderer2 to safely create and destroy the tooltip DOM node, and @Input to accept the tooltip text, position, and delay. As a standalone directive, it can be added to any component's imports array and used immediately with a single attribute on any element.
intro.usecase: Tooltips, clipboard-copy directives, infinite-scroll directives, and click-outside directives are the most common custom attribute directives in production Angular applications. Renderer2 instead of direct DOM manipulation is critical for SSR compatibility.

objectives: Create a standalone attribute directive with a selector in square brackets and apply it to any host element
Accept tooltip text, placement, and show-delay as @Input() properties with sensible defaults
Listen to mouseenter and mouseleave on the host element using @HostListener and manage show/hide timing with setTimeout
Create and position the tooltip DOM node using Renderer2.createElement() and Renderer2.appendChild() to remain SSR-safe
Destroy the tooltip node in ngOnDestroy and on mouseleave to prevent orphaned elements and memory leaks
Calculate viewport-aware position (flip from top to bottom when near the top edge) in the positioning logic
Write a test that simulates mouseenter and verifies the tooltip element appears in the DOM using a ComponentFixture
